newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Union says to close Georgetown operation.
newsitem.headline: Union says to close Georgetown operation.

text.p: Union Mining NL said on Wednesday it would close its small Georgetown gold mine in North Queensland in early June due to delays in the granting of new mining leases.
The company said it had sufficient gold resources on granted explortion permits to keep its operation going for up to five years, but the permits needed to be converted to mining leases.
Union, which processes ore carted in from satellite deposits at the Georgetown operation, produced 2,500 ounces of gold in the June quarter last year.
Union said it had experienced delays in the grant of mining leases last year due to environmental policy changes by the Department of Mines and Energy.
The grant of mining leases on pastoral land was then frozen following a High Court decision on native land title -- known as the Wik decision -- last December.
Although the freeze was recently lifted, the company said the time periods for the various procedures of the Native Title Act were too long to save its operation in the short-term.
The company said it would not know if there were respondents to its 15 mining lease applications until mid-June.
If there were respondents negotiations could go on for a further six months, possibly followed by arbitration, it said.
"Obviously this is an unworkable situation for the company and gives no long-term security to the project," Union said.
